- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% to account for momentum decay.
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.1) after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast slope slightly to capture sentiment-driven rally.
- Model underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (±0.3+ swings); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean to compensate for sentiment noise.
- When sentiment is flat or mildly negative, model tends to lag true price by 2–4 days; shift forecast forward by 1–2 days and increase early-week values by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum.
